Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: Boston Logan International Airport, Boston MA - Facility Tour
Tour-Category: facility

Stop 1: Terminal A Main Concourse

Address: 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3656, -71.0202

Type/Specialty: Airport Terminal

Specific Examples: Check-in counters, retail shops, dining options

Orientation: You are about to embark on a walking journey through Boston Logan International Airport, Boston MA. From the historic Terminal A Main Concourse, where St Mary's Cathedral was dedicated, to the modern Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium, witness the evolution of aviation infrastructure. Gustave Eiffel's Air Traffic Control Tower Base stands as a testament to the airport's rich history. Delve into the impact of connectivity and technology as seen in the transformation from the 18th-century marketplace by John Smibert to the bustling Faneuil Hall gifted by Peter Faneuil in 1742. At the upcoming stops, you will discover the link between the airport's growth and the Air Traffic Control Tower Base, which overlooks Logan International Airport. Additionally, you will learn about the community resistance in 1969 at the Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows. Your first stop is Terminal A Main Concourse. From the Airport T station, take the escalator up to the main terminal level. Follow the signs to Terminal A. You will notice the bustling atmosphere as travelers move about. Upon entering Terminal A's Main Concourse at Boston Logan International Airport, you'll immediately notice the expansive open space, filled with natural light filtering through the large windows.

Terminal A represents a significant milestone in airport design. This certification highlights the terminal's eco-friendly features, such as its sustainable roofing and advanced water systems, setting a precedent for environmentally conscious design in aviation. The airport itself has deep historical roots. In March 1922, Boston Mayor James Michael Curley approached Massachusetts Governor Channing H. Cox with a vision for a dedicated aviation field on the tidal mudflats of Jeffries Point in East Boston. This initiative was crucial in supporting civil commerce and national air defense, laying the groundwork for what would become Logan International Airport. Another fascinating episode in the airport's history involves Amelia Earhart. In 1928, she departed from Boston Airport for Newfoundland aboard the Friendship, ahead of her historic transatlantic flight. This moment marked a pivotal achievement in aviation history and cemented Boston's role as a key player in the development of international air travel. The Terminal A Main Concourse not only embodies sustainable design but also echoes the innovative spirit of early aviation pioneers. As you take in this bustling hub, consider the ongoing innovations that ensure the seamless operation of an airport that truly never sleeps.

Directions: As you exit Terminal A Main Concourse, head towards the parking garage. Walk past the airport shuttle pick-up area and continue towards the Control Tower Base. Follow the signs directing you to the Air Traffic Control Tower, and you'll soon arrive at your destination. Enjoy the stroll and the view of the planes taking off and landing as you make your way there.

Stop 2: Air Traffic Control Tower Base

Address: 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3657, -71.0205

Type/Specialty: Control Tower

Specific Examples: Views of air traffic operations, informational displays

Orientation: As you approach the Air Traffic Control Tower Base, you'll find yourself standing in the shadow of a monumental structure that has overseen the rhythms of Logan International Airport since its construction in 1973. Look up to see the Brutalist concrete design, a signature of architects Perry, Dean, Stahl & Rogers, marking a pivotal evolution in airport architecture.

The tower's cantilever bridge offers a dramatic visual line that captures the eye, a reminder of the critical role it plays in coordinating the intricate ballet of air traffic. The tower's history is intertwined with the growth of Logan International Airport, which spans over 2,384 acres and handles more than 43.5 million passengers annually. On April 23, 1969, the Massachusetts Port Authority cleared to extend Runway 15R/33L, resulting in the removal of dozens of historic mature trees. As you stand here, consider the tower's silent guardianship over the vast airfield, its presence a constant amid the airport's dynamic operations. This stop connects to the broader theme of the tour, highlighting Logan Airport as a hub of innovation and history, where the skies above are navigated with precision and care.

Directions: From the Air Traffic Control Tower Base, walk towards the Terminal C Departures. Head past the Terminal E Security Checkpoint and continue towards the Terminal E Gates. The Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows will be on your right, offering a great view of the runways.

Stop 3: Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows

Address: 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3660, -71.0210

Type/Specialty: Viewing Area

Specific Examples: Wide views of runways, seating areas, informational signage

Orientation: As you stand at the Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows, take a moment to appreciate the expanse of runways laid out before you. This vantage point offers a sweeping view that connects the airport's rich past with its present operations.

Here, the runways stretch over a landscape that once housed Wood Island Park. The transformation of this land set the stage for community resistance in 1969, as neighborhood mothers boldly blocked dump trucks with baby carriages. While witnessing the constant stream of incoming and outgoing flights, consider the pioneers of aviation. Charles Lindbergh and Amelia Earhart once soared above this very site, leaving their mark on the annals of history. This location not only provides a perspective on past aviation milestones but also reminds us of the constant evolution in air travel. As you observe the aircraft from different eras, imagine the future advancements that await the aviation industry.

Directions: As you leave the Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows, head towards the Airport Shuttle pick-up point near Terminal C. Continue walking through the tunnel connecting Terminals C and E. Once you emerge, stroll through the Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium, located just ahead on your right.

Stop 4: Terminal E Modernization Great Hall Atrium

Address: 1 Harborside Dr, Boston, MA 02128

Coordinates: 42.3663, -71.0215

Type/Specialty: Airport Terminal

Specific Examples: Modern architectural design, art installations, dining options

Orientation: As you step into the Great Hall Atrium of Terminal E at Boston Logan International Airport, pause near the central seating area for the best vantage point. The modern design surrounds you with sleek lines and open spaces, contrasting the bustling activity outside.

Terminal E's modernization, led by architect Luis Vidal and AECOM, transforms Logan into a major transatlantic gateway. This space, bustling with travelers from around the globe, stands on a site with roots in aviation history. Originally known as Jeffery Field, Boston Airport officially opened on September 8, 1923, primarily serving the U.S. Army Air Service and the Massachusetts National Guard. This early focus on military aviation underscored the airport's strategic importance, which has evolved into its current role as a hub for international travel. A significant historical event linked to this airport occurred on July 22, 1927, when the pioneering aviator Charles Lindbergh landed the Spirit of St. Louis here. After his historic solo transatlantic flight, Lindbergh embarked on a national tour to promote aviation. His arrival at Logan was met by tens of thousands who gathered to see the man who had crossed the Atlantic nonstop. This event marked a milestone in aviation history and highlighted the airport's emerging role in connecting America to the world. The transformation of Terminal E reflects a commitment to innovation and progress, echoing the spirit of those early days of aviation. The modernization project has expanded Logan's capacity and enhanced the passenger experience, aligning with the airport's legacy of connecting Boston to the global community. This stop, like the Panoramic Runway Viewing Windows you visited earlier, opens a window into the world of aviation, reminding us of the strides made since the days of Lindbergh. Here, the spirit of exploration and connectivity continues to define Boston Logan International Airport.

That's 4 stops — Terminal A Main Concourse, pivotal for civil commerce and air defense support and Air Traffic Control Tower Base, linked to Logan Airport's growth on 2,384 acres. If you would like to eat nearby we can build you a restaurant tour.
